markets.money_flow_note: Sympla collects buyer payments (Pix, card, boleto) and pays the producer automatically on the 3rd business day AFTER the event; fee is netted from the payout. Optional advance of up to 80% of confirmed sales for 3.49%.

plans.includes: Service fee 10% per ticket sold; tickets up to R$39.90 pay a fixed minimum R$3.99. No setup, no monthly, no adhesion fee. Check-in, attendee mgmt, ticket delivery included.
plans.notes: Producer chooses per event whether to absorb or pass the 10% to the buyer (must be set before publishing; locked after first sale). Plus a payment-processing fee of 2% to 2.5% per ticket (varies by Pix/card/boleto). Pricing page says processing cannot be passed on; the buyer help-centre article (updated 2026-10-05) says processing is ALWAYS paid by the buyer (worked example: R$100 absorbed -> buyer pays R$102.50, producer gets R$90.00; passed -> buyer pays R$112.75, producer gets R$100.00; R$30 passed -> buyer R$34.84). The two Sympla pages are therefore inconsistent.

plans.name: Seated events (lugar marcado)
plans.includes: Seat map events.

processing.rate_note: Processing 2% to 2.5% per ticket on top of the 10% service fee. Card installments up to 12x with interest of 3.49%/month paid by the buyer (third-party source, institutoitinerante.com.br, May 2026).

markets.free_tickets: Free events and free tickets: zero fee.
markets.payouts: Automatic payout on the 3rd business day after the event ends, to a registered bank account. Advance ('Adiantamento de repasse'): 3.49% of requested amount, 20/40/60/80% of confirmed sales, min R$300, request at least 4 days before the event, subject to Sympla risk approval, answer in up to 3 business days, funds within 1 business day. Not available for private or on-demand events.
markets.refunds_chargebacks: Buyer withdrawal right under Brazilian CDC (7 days, at least 48h before event). Complaints on Reclame Aqui indicate the service fee is not always refunded (not verified on Sympla's own page).
fine_print: Fee is configured per event BEFORE publishing; changing after sales start 'generates inconsistencies'

State laws override the pass-on option: Acre and Roraima ban any online convenience fee (producer must absorb, set automatically); Espirito Santo requires a no-fee alternative channel unless event <=200 people; Alagoas caps at 10% and requires no-fee sales points; Fortaleza 'Ingresso Justo' law requires one fee-free channel; Rio de Janeiro state law regulates fees
Half-price (meia-entrada) quota of 40% is mandatory by federal law 12.933/2013 (affects revenue, not the fee)
markets.enterprise: Consultant contact for seated events and volume; no public volume discounts.

sources.what: fee help article (updated 2026-10-05) with state laws and examples

notes: Brazil context: Pix is the dominant method. Convenience fee is legal (STJ) if disclosed up front; Procon-SP considers percentage-based fees abusive (should be fixed amount). Consumer-facing total of fees on big-event platforms is 10-20%+.

markets.money_flow_note: 'Recaudo gestionado' (BoletaDirecta collects, pays net 100% to any Colombian bank within 24 business hours after the event ends) vs 'Recaudo directo' (organizer's own payment gateway). Gateways cited: Wompi, Bold, Bancolombia, PSE. Price difference between the two modes not published.

plans.name: Direct (calculator)
plans.includes: Calculator on its own site shows '3% + COP 2,000 per ticket (Directo)'. The same page estimates TuBoleta ~10% + COP 3,000 and TicketExpress ~8% + COP 2,500 per ticket (marked 'est.', vendor assumptions).
plans.notes: The calculator's worked totals do not match its own formulas, so treat the numbers as indicative only.

markets.payouts: Managed collection: 24 business hours after the event; no '30 days waiting'.
fine_print: Organizer approval within 24 business hours
Direct-collection plan details at /partners not read

notes: Colombia: TuBoleta (market leader, ~65% share per its LinkedIn, negotiated per event with the promoter; service charge to buyer 10-15% of ticket value per El Tiempo 2023-10-13; no public producer rates). Eticket CO and Primerafila not found. Welcu also operates in Colombia (10% + taxes, see Welcu). Tikzet CO price COP 1,040 per ticket (see Tikzet). Joinnus operates in Colombia too but no CO terms were read.

segment: Peru's self-serve ticketing (Credicorp-owned), events of all sizes; also Colombia, Chile

markets.vat_note: Commission is '9% + IGV' (IGV = Peru VAT 18%) per ticket.
markets.money_flow_note: Inferred; the commercial agreement text read was truncated, payout terms not visible. Joinnus T&C: percentage of each ticket sold includes service access commission and the payment commission.

plans.name: Commercial agreement (2019 template)
plans.includes: Charge of 9% + IGV per ticket sold; organizer must show the Joinnus logo and purchase option in all communication.
plans.notes: From a Scribd copy of an old agreement ('Acuerdo Comercial (1).pdf'), so third_party and possibly outdated. Joinnus terms say it charges a percentage of each ticket that includes use commission and the payment-processor commission.

processing.rate_note: Payment commission is included in the percentage per its terms.

markets.refunds_chargebacks: Per event T&C (example Huaralino): refund limited to the price paid to the organizer.
fine_print: Rate comes from a 2019 sample contract

sources.what: page is JS-rendered, text only via search snippet

notes: Peru others: Teleticket (Ticket-collection agent for the organizer; commission included in the price and not published; organizer issues the receipt - https://teleticket.com.pe/paginas/TerminoCondiciones). Tickean's competitor page quotes 15% for Joinnus (vendor claim). Atrapalo PE not researched. Welcu and Tikzet operate in Peru (PEN 0.92 prepaid per ticket).

segment: Uruguay: RedTickets self-service (claims over half of events); Tickantel (Antel state telecom) for theatres/venues

markets.money_flow_note: RedTickets acts as mandatary 'on behalf of' the organizer (terms snippet), with 'Redpagos' physical points and crypto acceptance; no payout timing seen. Tickantel not opened.

plans.name: Not public
plans.includes: No producer fee published by either. Tikzet UY quotes UYU 10 per prepaid ticket (see Tikzet).
plans.notes: RedTickets terms page returned 403 to the reader; only the search snippet is known. A cooparte.uy article (2021) notes Tickantel exempted ticket-issue commission at box offices.

platform: Paraguay and Bolivia platforms (Fanz PY, RedTicket PY, Ticket Go BO, TicketBO)
segment: Smaller national platforms; one main self-serve per country as far as found

markets.vat_note: Fanz: IVA added on top of the commission.
markets.money_flow_note: Fanz settles to the organizer after 2, 10 or 20 days depending on plan (vendor claim).

plans.name: Fanz service charge
plans.includes: 8.26% + IVA paid by the buyer as service charge, no setup, no monthly; cost about PYG 10,890 on a PYG 100,000 ticket with debit card.
plans.notes: Own blog also says local market rates range 8% to 18% and Eventbrite ~6-18% per plan. Passline's PY rate 'not published'. RedTicket PY (new.redticket.com.py): 'small commission', no monthly cost, no setup fee, pays via Bancard QR, Pix, card, transfer; no numbers.

markets.payouts: 2, 10 or 20 days depending on plan (Fanz claim).
fine_print: Vendor-written comparison

markets.money_flow_note: Ticket Go terms are contradictory: the terms say ticket payment goes straight to the organizer's account, but its refund policy says Ticket Go receives and retains the payment and then pays the organizer minus its agreed commission. TicketBO says it takes no financial responsibility for the organizer's funds (suggests direct) but does not confirm.

plans.name: Ticket Go service fee
plans.includes: Price shown to buyer includes a service commission of Bs 10 per ticket; rotating anti-fraud QR, ID-card binding, offline validation.
plans.notes: Organizer commission 'agreed' but not published. TicketBO (ticket.bo) publishes no fees; QR bank payment.

markets.refunds_chargebacks: Ticket Go: organizer decides buyer refunds; TicketBO: organizer refunds within 30 days on cancellation.
fine_print: Very small platforms; terms dated July 2026

notes: Ecuador: no self-serve platform with public fees found (Ticketshow is a printed-ticket/collection business; terms not read). Uruguay is in the RedTickets entry.
